findings.title: tagDeviceUI caches the device before CreateOrUpdateDevice, bypassing the device limit on subsequent requests
findings.body: In `AnonDeviceService.tagDeviceUI`, `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` is called on line 87 before `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)` on line 93, and the cache key is not evicted when `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns an error. Because `Anonymous.Authenticate` now relies on `TagDevice` returning `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` to reject over-limit devices, a new device that exceeds the limit will fail on its first request, but its key will remain in `localCache` for the 29-minute TTL. Every subsequent request from that same device hits `a.localCache.Get(key)` on line 83 and returns `nil`, completely bypassing the device limit check. `a.localCache.SetDefault` should only be called after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds (and `untagDevice` should also evict the device key from `localCache`).

findings.title: updateDevice relies on RowsAffected() which returns 0 on MySQL when values do not change within the same second
findings.body: In `AnonDBStore.updateDevice`, when the device limit has been reached, an existing device is updated via `UPDATE anon_device SET client_ip = ?, user_agent = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE device_id = ? AND updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?` and `rowsAffected == 0` is treated as `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. In MySQL, `updated_at` has second precision (`DATETIME`) and `RowsAffected()` reports the number of rows whose values actually changed rather than rows matched. If an already-registered device issues concurrent requests within the same second with the same IP and User-Agent (for example, parallel requests during initial page load before `localCache` is populated), MySQL returns `0` rows affected and `updateDevice` falsely rejects the valid device with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. Additionally, line 81 computes the `BETWEEN` window from `device.UpdatedAt` instead of `time.Now()` as used in `CountDevices` on line 110.

findings.title: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit does not test that existing devices can still be updated at the limit
findings.body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` verifies that inserting a second device (`"keep"`) fails with `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when `deviceLimit` is 1, but it does not verify the other half of the contract: that calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice` again for the already-registered device (`"32mdo31deeqwes"`) succeeds and updates its record when the limit has been reached.
